texts.preamble: Municipal Corporation Of Greater ... vs Smita Sameer Bankar And Ors on 9 April, 2025 Hemant Chandersen 2025:Bhc-As:18457 Shiv H.C. Shiv Digitally signed by Hemant Chandersen Shiv Date: 2025.04.24 14:33:48 +0300 In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay Civil Appellate Jurisdiction First Appeal No.988 Of 2023 Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai Municipal Head Office, Mahapalika Marg, Mumbai 400 004 ...Appellant vs. 1. Smt. Smita Sameer Bankar
texts.facts: Present Appeal is filed by the Original Opposite Party aggrieved by the Judgment and Order dated 19th April 2022, in M.A.C.P. No.1799 of 2018, passed by the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Mumbai thereby the Appellant was directed to pay Respondent Nos.1 to 5 ("Claimants") the compensation of Rs.48,35,000/- alongwith interest @ 7.5% per annum from the date of claim till realisation of said entire amount. 2) The learned Advocate for the respective parties submitted that the Appeal may be finally heard at the stage of admission itself. Hence, the Appeal taken up for final hearing. 3) Facts giving rise to this Appeal are that, the claimants filed the said claim therein they averred that, on dated 24/09/2018, at about 1.30 hours, late Mr.Sameer Murlidhar Bankar ("deceased") was riding his motor scooter bearing MH-03-BV-5663 ("scooter") and he was proceeding by Sion Bridge, North Wahini road. When the scooter of the deceased reached at Mankikar junction, besides Highway Apartment, Sion, a motor dumper bearing regn. No.MH-01-AN-746 H.C. SHIV 16.fa988.23.doc ("dumper") gave a forcible dash to the scooter. The dumper was driven at a high speed and in a rash and negligent manner. As a result, the deceased fell down and sustained serious injuries. On receiving first information of the accident, Sion Police Station registered the same at FIR No.226/2018, under Sections 279 and 338 of IPC, against the driver of the dumper. The deceased died on the same day. 3.1) The claimants averred that, the deceased was doing a catering business thereby he was earning Rs.50,000/- per month. The claimants were dependent upon the income of the deceased. Therefore, they prayed to award a compensation of Rs.75,00,000/-. 4) The Appellant opposed the claim by filing the written statement (Exh.11) and denied that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the dumper. The Appellant denied that the deceased was doing the catering business and earning Rs.50,000/- per month. The Appellant contended that at the time and place of the accident, the deceased was riding his scooter at a high speed, rash and negligent manner and lost control while overtaking the dumper. As a result, the scooter skidded and came across the right rear wheel of the dumper. Consequently, the deceased suffered the fatal injuries. H.C. To prove the claim, the claimants adduced the evidence on Affidavit of Respondent No.1 (AW1/Exh.14) and Respondent No.5 (AW2/Exh.38). Besides, the claimants have relied upon various documents in evidence. In rebuttal, the Appellant produced the evidence of OW1-Vinod Pratap Sankpal, on Affidavit (Exh.42), who was driving the dumper at the relevant time. The deceased was doing the catering business thereby he was earning Rs.25,000/- per month. The claimants were dependent upon the deceased. Hence, the Appeal. Mr. Patil, therefore, submitted that the impugned judgment and order be modified accordingly. iv) Future General India Insurance Co. Ltd. Vs. Mumtaz Begum and Ors.4. In this case the deceased was running a Tea Stall with Snacks and Tiffing Centre. The Manager of the Tea Stall deposed that the profit of the Tea Stall would be Rs.25,000/- per month. There was no document to establish the same. There were no Income Tax Returns and there was no Bank Statement to establish such an amount of profit in the Tea Stall. The transaction of the Bank Statement revealed that the income was not clear. monthly income of the deceased was not established even through the Bank Statement. As such, there is no substance in the Appeal. The deceased died due to the said injuries. Since AW1 did not see the accident, her aforesaid narration was supported with the FIR (Exh.16), Spot Panchama (Exh.17), Inquest Panchnama (Exh.18) and Certificate as to the Cause of the Death (Exh.19). 10) At that point, a group of 8 to 10 bike riders, doing stunts, was heading from the opposite lane from Chembur to Sion. One of the stunt bikers contacted the scooter of the deceased. As a result, the deceased lost control and his scooter slipped. OW1 stated that then he heard a loud noise. So, he applied the brakes and alighted from the dumper. Then he saw that the deceased was lying under the right side rear wheel of the dumper, and he was seriously injured. OW1 contended that he was Municipal Corporation Of Greater ... vs Smita Sameer Bankar And Ors on 9 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190534095/ 4 not at fault in the accident. 10.1) In the cross-examination, OW1 admitted that he did not lodge a counter FIR. He did not place on record any document H.C. SHIV 16.fa988.23.doc contrary to the police statement. He did not refer the police statement of Respondent No.1, the Spot Panchnama or the Inquest Panchnama.
texts.arguments: 7) Mr. Patil, the learned Advocate for the Appellant submitted that the accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of the scooter by the deceased himself. In any event, this is case of contributory negligence, where the negligence on the part of the deceased was more. Mr.Patil, the learned Advocate submitted that apart from kachcha receipt and H.C. SHIV 16.fa988.23.doc registration certificate of Udyog Aadhar, the claimants have not produced any satisfactory documentary evidence to establish that, indeed the deceased was earning Rs.25,000/- per month by doing the catering business. According to him, the said income could be maximum Rs.15,000/-, notionally, as per minimum wages rules prevailing at the time of the accident. As such, the compensation awarded is on the higher side. 8) Mr.Mehta, the learned Advocate for the claimants, on the other hand, submitted that there is more than sufficient oral and documentary evidence by the claimants which clearly proved that the accident occurred only due to rash and negligent driving of the dumper. Therefore, the said driver stood prosecuted for said crime. Mr.Mehta submitted that the accident occurred in September 2018. The family of the deceased comprised of six members including the deceased. Compared to smaller towns and cities, the personal and living expenses of people living in Mumbai were on the higher side. However, Mr. Mehata submitted that in the absence of balance sheet like document, the said income may be taken as Rs.23,000/- per month, but not lesser than that.
